# Load human and chemical data

```{r}

#--------:HUMAN GENOME
hum <- fread(paste0(source_path, "CTD_human_genes_1.2.25.csv"))


#--------:CHEMICAL-GENE
chem <- fread(paste0(source_path, "CTD_chem_gene_ixns.8.7.25..csv")) #raw

```

# Human

```{r}
#1: Select columns for human gene list 
names(hum)[1]<- "gene_symbol"
names(hum)[2]<- "gene_name"

hum<-select(hum , 1:2)

#save
write.xlsx(hum, "G:/My Drive/Bakulski Lab/Projects/CTD-Dementia/data/CTD_human_genes_cleaned_1.2.25.xlsx")
```

# Chemical

```{r}
#2: Format/select chemical-gene interaction list 

#select relevant columns 
chem<- select(chem, 1:5, 7:8, 11)


#set column names
names(chem)[1]<- "chemical_name"
names(chem)[2]<- "chemical_id"
names(chem)[3]<- "casRN"
names(chem)[4]<- "gene_symbol"
names(chem)[5]<- "gene_id"
names(chem)[6]<- "organism"
names(chem)[7]<- "organism_id"
names(chem)[8]<- "pub_med_id"
names(chem)

#check number of unique chemicals 
length(unique(chem$chemical_name)) #15,167
#check<- chem %>% distinct(chemical_name) #15,167

```

## Apply filters: human genes only, non duplicate gene-chemical pairs

```{r}

#Filter chemical dataset for human genes only 
chem<- filter(chem, organism_id == 9606)
table(chem$organism_id, useNA = "always")
length(unique(chem$chemical_name))
check<- chem %>% distinct(chemical_name) #10,951



#filter chemical dataset set for non-duplicate chem-gene_symbol pairs
chem<- chem %>% select(gene_symbol, everything())
chem <-chem[!duplicated(chem[,1:2])]


#check
length(unique(chem$chemical_name))
length(unique(chem$chemical_id))
length(unique(chem$gene_symbol))


#double check
t= summary(chem$gene_symbol %in% hum$gene_symbol)
t=unique(chem$gene_symbol)
t=unique(chem$chemical_name)

#Cross check with human list to ensure we only have human
check_dis<-inner_join(humc, chem, by = "gene_symbol")  
rm(check_dis)

unique(length())
length(unique(chem$chemical_name))

```

## Save cleaned overall chemical dataset

```{r}
#save 
write.xlsx(chem, "G:/My Drive/Bakulski Lab/Projects/CTD-Dementia/data/CTD_chem_gene_ixns_cleaned_10.30.25.xlsx")

```

## Restrict cleaned chemical data to include those with \>= 50 genes

```{r}
#Load cleaned chemical dataset 
chem <- read.xlsx("G:/My Drive/Bakulski Lab/Projects/CTD-Dementia/data/CTD_chem_gene_ixns_cleaned_10.30.25.xlsx")


#count number of gene symbols per chemical 
agg_tbl <- chem %>% group_by(chemical_name) %>% 
  summarise(total_count=n(),
            .groups = 'drop')

#Restrict chemical list to those with >= 50 gene annotations 
agg_tbl1  <- filter(agg_tbl, total_count >= 50 )
length(unique(agg_tbl1$chemical_name)) #1008

mean(agg_tbl1$total_count)
min(agg_tbl1$total_count)
max(agg_tbl1$total_count)

#subset full list 
ge50_names = agg_tbl1$chemical_name
zes<-subset(chem, chemical_name %in% ge50_names)

#double check 
d<-unique(zes$chemical_name) #1008 - all good

#save
write.xlsx(zes, "G:/My Drive/Bakulski Lab/Projects/CTD-Dementia/data/CTD_chem_GE50_genes_10.30.25.xlsx")

```

# Convert format human, chemical, and disease dataframes to list for analysis

## Human

```{r}

#HUMAN GENE LIST
hum <- read.xlsx(paste0(source_path, "CTD_human_genes_cleaned_1.2.25.xlsx"))

#select relevant columns only for each data set
HU <- select(hum, 1)

#Save each data frame as a list for easier manipulation 
HU<- as.list(HU)

#Set column name of human gene list
#Allows us to access information within the list easier
names(HU) <- c("Hum")

#save and load into analysis file 
    saveRDS(HU, file = "human_gene_list_11.3.25_list.rds")

```

## Format chemical

```{r}

#CHEMICAL GENE LIST 
chem<- read.xlsx(paste0(source_path, "CTD_chem_GE50_genes_10.30.25.xlsx")) 

#select relevant columns only for each data set
CH <- select(chem, 1,2)

#Save each data frame as a list for easier manipulation 
#Split chem data frame by chemical name & saves as list
#CG:shows each chemical and number of unique gene_symbols 
CG <- split(CH, f = CH$chemical_name) 

#save and load into analysis file 
    saveRDS(CG, file = "chemical_gene_list_analytic_11.3.25.rds")
```
